svg.text: One shot, 800 m, on the game's own map
.308 Win in desert air, zeroed at 100 m, a 10 mph (4.47 m/s) wind from the left. Terrain and bullet path are the game's real data (desert map, ridge position).
Seen from above: the wind pushes the bullet sideways
map at true scale (220 m across); the bullet's sideways movement is drawn ×25 so it can be seen
Seen from the side: gravity and drag pull the bullet down
line of sight to the aim point (straight)
heights drawn ×14 (the ridge is 12 m high, the target 800 m away)
Flight: 1.43 s, arriving at 393 m/s (Mach 1.11). Sound: the target hears the shot 2.26 s after it is fired, 0.83 s after the bullet has already arrived.
Without air the bullet would reach 800 m in 1.01 s and fall only 5.0 m: drag slows it, so it spends longer falling. The wind drift equals 4.47 m/s × (1.434 s − 800/790 s) = 1.89 m, the lag rule.
